parsed_output.authors_year: Hongfu Liu, Junxiang Chen, Jennifer Dy, and Yun Fu, 2023
parsed_output.research_question: How can available approaches in generalizing K-means be unified to solve challenging and complex non-standard cluster analysis problems?
parsed_output.context: K-means is widely used due to its simplicity and efficiency, and standard K-means is equivalent to PCA, NMF, and spectral clustering under squared Euclidean distance. This survey paper focuses on generalizing K-means regarding data input, distance measure, label assignment, and centroid updating to solve complex non-standard cluster analysis problems.
methods: Data transformation to convert problem domains into modified K-means formulations
Utilizing generalized distance functions such as Bregman divergences and Point-to-Centroid (P2C) distance
Employing non-exhaustive and overlapping label assignment strategies (e.g. K-means– and NEO-K-means)
Applying incomplete centroid updating rules to handle missing elements or auxiliary zero fill-ups
main_findings: Iterative subspace projection and clustering can be solved via kernel K-means with a specific kernel Gram matrix.
Utility-based consensus clustering can be formulated and solved efficiently using K-means on a binary matrix formed by one-hot encoding basic partitions.
Spectral ensemble clustering can be transformed into a weighted K-means clustering, reducing time and space complexities from O(n^3) and O(n^2) to O(n).
Partition level constrained clustering can be modeled as K-means by concatenating the feature matrix with side information and auxiliary zeros.
Structure-preserved unsupervised domain adaptation uses a partition-level constrained clustering framework under K-means.
Joint clustering and outlier detection (COR) can be solved via K-means– by transforming the original space into partition space and employing Holoentropy.
assumptions: The centroid updating or calculation must match the K-means distance to guarantee algorithmic convergence.
Auxiliary zero fill-ups in concatenated matrices do not contribute to distance calculations or centroid updates.
limitations_explicit: K-means fails to capture non-spherical cluster structures due to the prototypical assumption.
K-means performance is heavily affected by the sensitivity of initialization.
Almost every clustering algorithm, including K-means, requires pre-defined parameters such as the cluster number K.

potential_open_questions.evidence: Table I and Section III-B note that cosine similarity is a widely used metric in high-dimensional clustering, however, this cannot be generalized into Bregman divergence.

candidate_hypotheses.rationale: Mapping original feature spaces or co-association matrices into binary indicator matrices converts high-complexity spectral problems into sparse weighted K-means formulations solvable by Lloyd's algorithm.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: Section IV-C and Section IV-F show that spectral ensemble clustering and clustering with outlier removal achieve O(n) complexity and competitive empirical performance by operating in the transformed partition space.

parsed_output.authors_year: Tiziano Iannaccio and Maurizio Vichi, 2026
parsed_output.research_question: How to establish a universal, domain-agnostic definition of an outlier with a probabilistic interpretation that replaces heuristic trimming quotas in objective-based clustering algorithms like K-means?
parsed_output.context: Outlier detection is critical for statistical modeling, machine learning, and exploratory data analysis. Existing approaches frequently rely on heuristic trimming quotas that lack statistical interpretations and are difficult to tune, while standard K-means is sensitive to outliers unless robustified.
methods: Formulating a pseudo-isolation outlier score using weighted nearest-neighbor Mahalanobis distances starting from a rank h >= 1.
Applying the Cantelli (unilateral Chebyshev) inequality on running sample estimators of pseudo-isolations to establish a probabilistic outlier threshold linked to a false-alarm rate alpha.
Integrating the outlier detection module into K-means to create Outlier Detection K-means (ODK-means) as a weighted extension of K-means.

Developing an inverse inference framework (alpha-star search and packet-boundary search) to evaluate the minimum false-alarm rate required to flag a given observation and analyze coalescence properties.
main_findings: ODK-means successfully provides adaptive outlier trimming with a rigorous false-alarm rate alpha, outperforming Trimmed K-means and Local Outlier Factor (LOF) across various simulated contamination rates and dispersion levels.

The outlier topology exhibits three main properties: Quiescence, Class Equivalence, and Coalescence (showing that outliers move in coalescence groups rather than separating individually at every possible threshold).
ODK-means natively reduces to standard K-means when no anomalies are detected, avoiding the logical paradox present in Trimmed K-means when setting trimming proportions to zero.
assumptions: The underlying pseudo-isolation score distribution has finite sample mean and variance.
Standard asymptotic k-NN theory applies, setting neighborhood parameter l such that l -> infinity and l/N -> 0 as N -> infinity.
limitations_explicit: ODK-means inherits the limitations of standard K-means regarding cluster geometries unless combined with clustering algorithms robust to general geometries (e.g., Gaussian-mixture models).

The framework relies on a purely methodological perspective, and developing a fully parametric extension to derive a closed-form distribution for the pseudo-isolation score remains open for future research.

potential_open_questions.question: Can a fully parametric extension of this framework derive an exact closed-form distribution for the pseudo-isolation score?
potential_open_questions.why_unresolved: The current framework is built on nonparametric running sample estimators and Cantelli bounds rather than an exact closed-form distribution under specific parametric assumptions.
potential_open_questions.evidence: We conclude this work by pointing to the main direction for future research: developing a fully parametric extension of this framework to derive a closed-form distribution for the pseudo-isolation score. (Section 8)

potential_open_questions.question: How can the optimization of neighborhood ranks (h, l) for pseudo-isolation be rigorously formalized?
potential_open_questions.why_unresolved: The selection of neighborhood ranks relies on standard asymptotic k-NN theory conventions rather than an explicit optimization routine.
potential_open_questions.evidence: Remark 3 The optimization of the neighborhood ranks (h, l) is beyond the scope of this work. Throughout this manuscript, we adhere to standard asymptotic k-NN theory... (Section 3.1)

parsed_output.paper_title: Adaptive Federated Baseline K-Means for Lightweight IoT Intrusion Detection: Auto-Thresholding and Robust Statistics Aggregation
parsed_output.authors_year: Mohammed Al Saleh and Joseph Azar, 2026
parsed_output.research_question: How can the merge-induced precision decay and manual thresholding of the federated Baseline K-Means (BKM) detector be repaired for lightweight IoT intrusion detection while preserving its statistics-only and semi-supervised identity?
parsed_output.context: Federated, semi-supervised novelty detection is well-suited for resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) nodes where benign traffic is abundant and sharing raw data is precluded. A previously published cross-layer federated detector (Baseline K-Means) raised collaborative recall over time but exhibited a structural side effect: after every merge, precision decayed and the false-positive rate (FPR) climbed due to coordinator recomputation of the threshold filtered by the closest observed anomaly, combined with manual percentile tuning.
methods: Developing AF-BKM (Adaptive Federated Baseline K-Means) incorporating E1 (adaptive auto-thresholding via a robust median-absolute-deviation rule or target-FPR calibration, removing manual percentile search) and E2 (robust, benignly anchored aggregation blending worker means under count and quality weighting behind a trust gate, and recalibrating the threshold on a trusted benign anchor)
Evaluating on three public datasets (NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and the commercial IoT N-BaIoT corpus) using a non-IID federated protocol with baseline-only MinMax scaling and label-blind feature filtering

Performing a four-way ablation study, statistical significance testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank test across 10 seeds), heterogeneity and scale sweeps, adversarial stress tests (faulty-worker updates, anchor contamination, and white-box evasion), and a computational resource profiling
main_findings: AF-BKM successfully removes the merge-induced precision decay, improving the first-to-last-epoch precision change from −0.134 to −0.002 on NSL-KDD, from −0.121 to −0.014 on UNSW-NB15, and from −0.170 to −0.009 on N-BaIoT.
Mean FPR is reduced by 30-64% depending on the dataset, with improvements statistically significant across 10 seeds (p = 0.002, large effect sizes).
AF-BKM preserves recall on NSL-KDD and N-BaIoT, and exposes an explicit precision-recall trade-off through a benign target-FPR knob on the harder UNSW-NB15 dataset.

The deployed model serializes to 5.5-52 KB, classifies a packet in 11-27 microseconds on a benchmark desktop CPU, and uploads a compact d+3-value summary (160-472 bytes) per merge round, saving 94.6-98.3% compared to sharing covariance matrices.
assumptions: The system is label-free regarding attack labels, requiring no attack labels for thresholding or worker-quality weighting.
There exists a small, trusted benign anchor collected during device commissioning for benign-only calibration.
The coordinator stores the anchor securely and is not compromised, so operational traffic cannot modify the anchor after commissioning.
limitations_explicit: The false-positive level is anchor-relative rather than local when a worker's benign distribution drifts far from the trusted benign anchor.
Under the MAD default, the false-positive level is a stable level rather than an operator-chosen target, and it assumes secure coordinator storage of the anchor.
The non-IID setting primarily models label skew with a small viability floor, leaving feature-space skew, per-device behavioral drift, and changing traffic mixtures for deeper treatment.
The study reports desktop CPU timing, Python-traced peak allocation, and closed-form fp32 serialization sizes, including no new physical edge deployment or direct energy measurements.

The robustness evaluation covers selected faulty-worker updates, anchor contamination, and white-box evasion, establishing no worst-case guarantees and omitting adaptive adversaries that jointly optimize against the trust gate, blend, and anchor.

potential_open_questions.question: How can the federated framework be extended to dynamically adapt to streaming concept drift over long operational deployments?
potential_open_questions.why_unresolved: The current framework assumes the benign calibration remains static relative to the initial anchor and implements no streaming concept-drift mechanism.
potential_open_questions.evidence: Footnote † and Section 7 note that AF-BKM adapts its threshold to the benign distance distribution but implements no streaming concept-drift mechanism, leaving drift adaptation to future work.

potential_open_questions.question: Can robust covariance estimators (such as the minimum-covariance-determinant estimator) eliminate the sensitivity of the Gaussian model to commissioning-anchor contamination?
potential_open_questions.why_unresolved: While the threshold rule survives contamination, the sample mean and covariance underneath it are not robust estimators, leading to recall loss when attack rows contaminate the initial anchor window.
potential_open_questions.evidence: Section 6.7 and Section 7.4 state that planted attack rows inflate the covariance along attack directions, shrinking attack distances and costing recall, which argues for robust estimators like MCD as a hardening step.

candidate_hypotheses.hypothesis: Replacing nearest-anomaly threshold tightening with a benignly anchored recalibration rule removes merge-induced precision decay across diverse IoT intrusion detection datasets.
candidate_hypotheses.rationale: The structural root cause of precision decay is the coordinator rule tightening the threshold toward the nearest worker-reported anomaly after every merge. Benignly anchoring the threshold to a trusted anchor prevents this progressive tightening.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: Ablation results in Section 6.1 and Table 4 demonstrate that robust aggregation (E2 and AF-BKM) flattens the precision curve (delta P approx -0.002 on NSL-KDD) while keeping FPR low.

candidate_hypotheses.hypothesis: Using a robust median-absolute-deviation (MAD) threshold rule instead of a manual percentile search provides a search-free, stable decision threshold that maintains high F1 scores across datasets.
candidate_hypotheses.rationale: Manual percentiles are dataset-dependent and unknowable a priori, whereas data-driven dispersion statistics like MAD characterize the benign distance distribution without requiring search or labels.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence: Section 6.2 and Table 6 show that search-free rules like MAD land close to the best manual percentile on NSL-KDD and N-BaIoT and provide stable operating points.

parsed_output.historical_analysis: The evolution of outlier trimming and robust variants within K-means and similar partitive clustering algorithms has progressed from early asymptotic investigations and non-robust formulations (MacQueen 1967) to combinatorial impartial trimming strategies (Cuesta-Albertos et al. 1997; García-Escudero et al. 2003; Cuesta-Albertos et al. 2008), regularization-based robust optimization and proximal maps (Georgogiannis 2016), centroid update thresholding rules (Olukanmi and Twala 2017; Shrifan et al. 2022; Liu et al. 2021), continuous weight relaxations and simplex constraints (Dorabiala et al. 2022), and advanced nonparametric pseudo-isolation or federated anomaly-aware aggregation architectures (Iannaccio and Vichi 2026; Al Saleh and Azar 2026). Despite these extensive developments, major challenges persist regarding breakdown limits, data-driven parameterization of trimming and neighborhood thresholds, generalization to arbitrary non-spherical or high-dimensional spaces, and robust handling of distributed concept drift.

research_gaps.gap: Handling streaming concept drift and local distribution shifts in federated outlier-aware clustering frameworks
research_gaps.why_it_matters: In practical federated or decentralized IoT deployments, device behaviors and local network traffic patterns drift continuously over time. Without dynamic drift adaptation, static commissioning-anchor calibration leads to rising false positive rates or missed anomalies.
research_gaps.what_is_known: AF-BKM repairs merge-induced precision decay and automates thresholding via robust statistics and a trusted benign anchor during initial commissioning.
research_gaps.what_remains_unknown: How the federated framework can dynamically adapt to streaming concept drift over long operational deployments without requiring frequent manual recalibration.

related_papers.explanation: Al Saleh and Azar (2026) acknowledge that AF-BKM implements no streaming concept-drift mechanism and leaves continuous drift adaptation for future work.

evidence.evidence: AF-BKM adapts its threshold to the benign distance distribution but implements no streaming concept-drift mechanism, leaving drift adaptation to future work.

research_gaps.gap: Resilience of commissioning anchors against poisoning and contamination via robust multivariate covariance estimators
research_gaps.why_it_matters: If initial commissioning data contains subtle or planted malicious/anomalous rows, standard sample means and covariances inflate along attack directions, distorting the trust gate and shrinking attack distances which degrades outlier recall.
research_gaps.what_is_known: Threshold rules and benign blending rules provide robustness during worker aggregation, but the underlying distribution statistics depend on the initial anchor.
research_gaps.what_remains_unknown: Whether robust covariance estimators such as minimum-covariance-determinant (MCD) can eliminate the sensitivity of Gaussian-based distance thresholds to initial anchor contamination.

related_papers.explanation: Discusses how planted attack rows inflate covariance and propose robust estimators like MCD as a hardening step.

evidence.evidence: Planted attack rows inflate the covariance along attack directions, shrinking attack distances and costing recall, which argues for robust estimators like MCD as a hardening step.

research_gaps.gap: Parametric closed-form derivations for pseudo-isolation outlier scoring distributions in clustering frameworks
research_gaps.why_it_matters: Current nonparametric implementations rely on running sample estimators and Cantelli bounds, making it difficult to analyze exact finite-sample tail behaviors and tail probabilities without empirical approximation.
research_gaps.what_is_known: ODK-means uses weighted nearest-neighbor Mahalanobis distances and pseudo-isolation scores coupled with Cantelli inequalities to establish probabilistic outlier thresholds.
research_gaps.what_remains_unknown: Whether a fully parametric extension can be developed to derive an exact closed-form distribution for pseudo-isolation scores under specific underlying data distributions.

related_papers.explanation: Iannaccio and Vichi (2026) explicitly point to developing a fully parametric extension to derive closed-form score distributions as a primary future research direction.

evidence.evidence: We conclude this work by pointing to the main direction for future research: developing a fully parametric extension of this framework to derive a closed-form distribution for the pseudo-isolation score.

parsed_output.historical_analysis: Research on outlier trimming and robust clustering within K-means and related paradigms has evolved from classical geometric formulations and combinatorial approaches to modern probabilistic, non-parametric, and decentralized federated architectures. Early foundations like MacQueen (1967) established standard k-means partitioning, while Cuesta-Albertos et al. (1997) introduced trimmed k-means with impartial trimming and consistency proofs. Subsequent works expanded trimming into exploratory data analysis (García-Escudero et al., 2003) and robust variations (Georgogiannis, 2016). Recent years have seen the development of diverse specialized variants, including modified centroid updates with MAD thresholds (Olukanmi and Twala, 2017), sampling-based distributed algorithms with theoretical guarantees (Grunau and Rozhon, 2022), continuous simplex relaxations for multi-membership and outlier detection (Dorabiala et al., 2022), algebraic and rule-based attribute trimming (Shrifan et al., 2022), and advanced algebraic transformations (Liu et al., 2023). Most recently, research has moved toward adaptive non-parametric frameworks like ODK-means using pseudo-isolation scores and Cantelli bounds (Iannaccio and Vichi, 2026), alongside federated outlier-aware clustering architectures equipped with auto-thresholding and robust baseline aggregations (Al Saleh and Azar, 2026). Despite these advancements, significant research gaps remain regarding parameter estimation, convergence behaviors, and adaptation under complex streaming or non-Euclidean environments.

Without automated data-driven estimation, practical deployment is hindered in dynamic environments where these proportions are unknown beforehand.
